newsitem.title: JAPAN: Economy recovering but tax rise having effect - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Economy recovering but tax rise having effect - BOJ.

text.p: The Japanese economy is maintaining its gradual recovery trend although some effects of the sales tax rise on April 1 are being seen in some parts of the economy, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday.

Matsushita said repercussions from "rush in" demand ahead of the rise in the sales tax were seen in parts of the economy but added: "Basically, a gradual recovery trend is continuing on the back of firmness in capital spending."
He said this assessment of the economy was reached taking into account discussions after a two-day meeting of BOJ branch managers on Monday and Tuesday.

Matsushita said that while public spending continued to decrease, net exports were on a rising trend. Some smaller firms were still cautious in their capital spending, but overall, corporate profits were increasing.
Matsushita said private consumption had fallen in April in reaction to the "rush in" demand in March ahead of the tax rise, but said the fall was within expectations.
He added that time was still needed to judge the effects of the tax rise on the overall economy.

Production was continuing to rise and the declining trend in prices was clearly coming to a halt. Taking into account positive signs in production, incomes and spending, it was highly likely that the economic recovery would continue despite the negative effects from fiscal tightening measures such as the tax rise.

Foreign exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals, Matsushita said. He added that the central bank would continue to monitor the effects of the yen's weakening on domestic prices, although he did not expect prices to show any signs of rising soon.
Matsushita said the depreciation of the yen along with strong overseas economies had led to a gradual increase in Japan's current account surplus.
But a rise in imports brought about by structural changes in Japan's economy and the economic recovery itself would work to suppress the rising trend in the current account surplus.
He said money supply growth was in line with the economy.
"Money supply is in balance with the conditions of the real economy," he said.
Japan's broadly defined money supply of M2 plus CDs (certificates of deposit) grew 2.7 percent in March from a year earlier, down from 3.0 percent in February.
